answers.question: Within how many minutes must a mine operator call MSHA after an accident that kills a miner?
answers.answer: A mine operator must contact MSHA within 15 minutes after a death occurs at the mine. Per 30 CFR 50.10, the operator must immediately contact MSHA "at once without delay and within 15 minutes" once it knows or should know that an accident involving a death has occurred.

claims.text: The operator must immediately contact MSHA without delay and within 15 minutes once it knows or should know an accident involving a death has occurred.
claims.quote: The operator shall immediately contact MSHA at once without delay and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number, 1-800-746-1553, once the operator knows or should know that an accident has occurred involving:

claims.text: A death of an individual at the mine is one of the accident types requiring this immediate notification.
claims.quote: (a) A death of an individual at the mine;

answers.question: What minimum incombustible content must the combined dust in an underground coal mine keep where no methane is present?
answers.answer: Where methane is not present, the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust in underground areas of a coal mine must be maintained so that the incombustible content is not less than 80 percent.

claims.text: The incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be maintained at not less than 80 percent where rock dust is required to be applied.
claims.quote: Where rock dust is required to be applied, it shall be distributed upon the top, floor, and sides of all underground areas of a coal mine and maintained in such quantities that the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent.

answers.question: How long must the self-rescue device given to each underground coal miner be able to protect that person?
answers.answer: The self-rescue device provided to each underground coal miner must be adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.

claims.text: Each operator shall make available to each miner who goes underground an approved self-rescue device or devices adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.
claims.quote: Each operator shall make available to each miner who goes underground, and to visitors authorized to enter the mine by the operator, an approved self-rescue device or devices which is adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.

answers.question: How often must an underground metal or nonmetal mine hold evacuation drills?
answers.answer: For underground metal and nonmetal mines, evacuation drills must be held at least once every six months.

claims.text: Underground metal/nonmetal mine evacuation drills must be held at least once every six months.
claims.quote: At least once every six months, mine evacuation drills shall be held to assess the ability of all persons underground to reach the surface or other designated points of safety within the time limits of the self-rescue devices that would be used during an actual emergency.

answers.question: How many hours of training must a new underground miner receive before being assigned to work duties?
answers.answer: A new (underground) miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties.

claims.text: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training as prescribed before being assigned to work duties.
claims.quote: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training as prescribed in this section before such miner is assigned to work duties.

answers.question: What is the permissible exposure level for noise at a mine, as an 8-hour average?
answers.answer: The permissible exposure level for noise at a mine, expressed as an 8-hour time-weighted average (TWA8), is 90 dBA (equivalent to a noise dose of 100%), integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA.

claims.text: Permissible exposure level is a TWA8 of 90 dBA, or equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard, integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA.
claims.quote: Permissible exposure level. A TWA8 of 90 dBA or equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard, integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA.

answers.question: How high must berms or guardrails be on the banks of roadways at metal and nonmetal mines?
answers.answer: At metal and nonmetal mines, berms or guardrails on the banks of roadways must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment that usually travels the roadway.

claims.text: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

claims.text: The same mid-axle height requirement applies under the parallel underground metal and nonmetal mine standard.
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

answers.question: For how many hours must the breathable air in an approved refuge alternative sustain each person?
answers.answer: The breathable air supplied within a refuge alternative must sustain each person for 96 hours.

claims.text: The breathable air shall sustain each person for 96 hours.

answers.question: What must a written bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan contain under OSHA?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not contain any information about OSHA's bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan requirements. The chunks available only address MSHA (30 CFR) topics such as respirable dust control plans, MSDS contents, and quality control plans for fuses—none of which pertain to bloodborne pathogens exposure control plans under OSHA.

answers.question: At what depth does OSHA require a construction trench to have a protective system such as shoring or a trench box?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not contain any information about OSHA's trench safety requirements or the depth at which a protective system (such as shoring or a trench box) is required in construction trenches. The chunks instead cover MSHA (30 CFR) regulations on mine shaft sinking, hoist buckets, overhead protection for shaft deepening, and coal mine slope/shaft plan approval — none of which address OSHA construction trenching standards.

answers.question: What FAA certification does a pilot need to fly a drone over a mine site?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not contain any information about FAA certification requirements for pilots flying drones over mine sites. They only cover mine map certification, mine foreman/examiner certification, electric face equipment permits, and surface facilities waivers under CFR 30 mining regulations.

answers.question: When does a mine need an EPA stormwater discharge permit for runoff from its site?
answers.answer: The provided regulatory text does not address EPA stormwater discharge permits for runoff from mine sites. The chunks available only cover permits for mining operations conducted under rivers, streams, lakes, or other bodies of water (30 CFR § 75.1716 and related sections), which concern cave-in hazards to miners, not stormwater runoff or EPA permitting requirements.
